note: The last release that went out, and the newest entry in runtime/release-history.json. Android installs an update only with this package, this signing certificate and a higher versionCode; scripts/verify-upgrade-compatibility.sh enforces all three in the release job. It records the first release (0.1, versionCode 1), which is why every later build is already above it. signerSha256 is empty until it is taken from the key that release was signed with: run scripts/verify-upgrade-compatibility.sh <published apk> --emit <file> with that APK, or paste the SHA-256 apksigner verify --print-certs prints, into this file and the same release's entry in the history, then delete signerPending. While it is empty a release signed by a different key is not caught, so signerPending marks the exemption: --emit never writes it, the preflight warns while it is set, and tools/check-release-history.py refuses a baseline that has no certificate and no exemption, or one that has both.
